title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
subtitle: Crunchy chilled cucumber with a punchy sesame and chilli dressing
excerpt: Smashing the cucumbers rather than slicing them creates jagged edges that catch more dressing. A short rest in the fridge lets the flavours deepen. This is a crisp, refreshing side that works alongside almost anything.
sourceNotes: Pai huang gua, smashed cucumber salad, is a classic Sichuan cold dish found throughout northern and western China. The smashing technique is centuries old and helps cucumbers absorb dressings far better than clean-cut slices.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dress up to 1 hour ahead and keep chilled.

content.text: Use the flat side of a large knife or the bottom of a heavy mug to smash the cucumbers. Break them into irregular chunks rather than trying to cut neatly.
Trim the ends from the cucumbers. Place each cucumber on a chopping board and smash firmly along its length using the flat side of a large knife or a rolling pin.
Break into roughly 3 cm pieces and place in a colander. Toss with half a teaspoon of salt and leave for 10 minutes. This draws out excess water.
Whisk together the garlic, rice vinegar, sesame oil, soy sauce, chilli flakes and gochugaru in a large bowl.
Pat the cucumber dry. Add to the dressing and toss to coat. Scatter over the spring onion.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Salad is watery and dressing is diluted.
items.cause: The cucumber was not salted and drained before dressing.
items.fix: Salt and drain cucumber for 10 minutes before mixing.

items.cause: Too much vinegar or raw garlic is overwhelming.
items.fix: Add a small pinch of sugar to balance the vinegar.
